'''Marc Davis''' (born September 8, 1947)<ref name=spacenews>{{cite web|title=Dannie Heineman Prizes for 2006|url=https://spacenews.com/dannie-heineman-prizes-for-2006/|publisher=SpaceNews|date=2006-01-31|access-date=2026-10-18}}</ref> is an American professor of [[astronomy]] and [[physics]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name=Gruber>{{cite web|title=2011 Cosmology Prize: Marc Davis|url=https://gruber.yale.edu/cosmology/marc-davis|work=Gruber prizes|publisher=The Gruber Foundation|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140512222307/http://gruber.yale.edu/cosmology/marc-davis|archive-date=2014-05-12|access-date=2026-10-18}}</ref> Davis received his bachelor's degree from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1969, his PhD from [[Princeton University]] in 1973 and has been elected to both the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] (1991) and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1992). He taught for a year at Princeton, 1973–1974, then was on the astronomy faculty at [[Harvard University]] from 1975 to 1981. Since 1981, he has been on the faculty of the Department of Astronomy and Physics at the University of California at Berkeley.

== Career ==
Davis' work has been in [[physical cosmology]] and he has done a number of significant projects. While at Harvard, he led the CfA ([[Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics|Center for Astrophysics, Harvard & Smithsonian]]) galaxy [[Astronomical survey|survey]], the first [[redshift survey]] of galaxies,<ref>{{cite book|title=The Vindication of the Big Bang: Breakthroughs and Barriers|first=Barry|last=Parker|publisher=Plenum Press|date=1993|location=New York}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Huchra|first=John|url=https://lweb.cfa.harvard.edu/~dfabricant/huchra/zcat/|title=THE CfA REDSHIFT SURVEY|access-date=2026-10-18}}</ref> which motivated his interest in [[N-body simulation]]s of the Universe. In the 1980s, at Berkeley, he was part of a collaboration with [[George Efstathiou]], [[Carlos Frenk]] and [[Simon White]] that established the validity of the "[[cold dark matter]]" theory for the [[formation of galaxies]] and other cosmic structures, now the accepted interpretation in cosmology. In a series of nine papers published between 1984 and 1992, that collaboration (often referred to as DEFW<ref name=Gruber /><ref name=nbc>{{cite web|author=SPACE.com Staff|title=Astronomers Nab $500,000 Prize for Hunting Elusive Dark Matter|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna43257929|website=NBC News|date=2011-06-02|access-date=2026-10-18}}</ref>) used computer code to simulate the growth of the universe and resolve disputes among theoretical models.

Through the 1990s, Davis worked on the theoretically expected large scale flow of galaxies and led the redshift survey of the first all-sky catalog, [[IRAS]], with which he was able to estimate the flow of galaxies out to redshifts of order 6,000 km/s. He took up this project once again in 2010 using the gravity field estimated from [[2MASS]], and he and Adi Nusser were able to estimate the field to redshift of order 10,000 km/s.

He published a widely-used [[Milky Way|Galactic]] [[Dust#Outer_space|dust]] map in 1998, with [[David J. Schlegel]] and [[Douglas P. Finkbeiner]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Schlegel|first1=David J.|last2=Finkbeiner|first2=Douglas P.|last3=Davis|first3=Marc|date=1998|title=Maps of Dust Infrared Emission for Use in Estimation of Reddening and Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation Foregrounds|journal=[[The Astrophysical Journal]]|volume=500|issue=2|pages=525-553|doi= 
10.1086/305772|arxiv=astro-ph/9710327}}</ref> The map provided estimates of Galactic [[extinction (astronomy)|reddening]] and the dust-related contamination of [[cosmic microwave background]] measurements.

He was the lead principal investigator on the ambitious [[DEEP2 Redshift Survey]] of 50,000 high redshift galaxies. This was conducted on the {{convert|10|m}} [[W. M. Keck Observatory]] in [[Hawaii]]. The scientific goals of the DEEP survey were to study the properties of galaxies and the clustering of galaxies as the universe has evolved.

== Honors and awards ==
Davis was awarded an honorary PhD from the University of Chicago in 2008. He has also been named a fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science<ref>{{cite journal|journal=University of California Bulletin |date=August 6–10, 1984|volume=33|issue=3|title=American Association for the Advancement of Science Elects University Members|page=12|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2vM2AQAAMAAJ&pg=PA12 |via=Google Books}}</ref> and the [[American Physical Society]], and he has received the [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Astrophysics]] from the American Institute of Physics and the American Astronomical Society,<ref name=Heineman>{{cite web|title=Dannie Heineman Prize for Astrophysics|url=https://aas.org/about/grants-and-prizes/dannie-heineman-prize-astrophysics|work=Grants and Prizes|publisher=[[American Astronomical Society]]|accessdate=8 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160121053552/http://aas.org/about/grants-and-prizes/dannie-heineman-prize-astrophysics|archive-date=21 January 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> as well as the [[Gruber Prize in Cosmology]] in 2011,<ref name=Gruber/><ref>{{cite press release |last=Sanders |first=Robert |date=1 June 2011 |title=Gruber Cosmology Prize honors 'dark matter' astronomers |url=https://newscenter.berkeley.edu/2011/06/01/gruber-cosmology-prize-honors-dark-matter-astronomers/ |publisher=University of California Berkeley |accessdate=2014-05-08}}</ref> among numerous other prizes and awards.

== Stroke ==
While working on the DEEP survey, Davis suffered a stroke in June 2003, which has affected his right limbs, although he continues to enjoy one of the main passions in his life, skiing.<ref>{{cite news|last=Magid|first=Marian |title=Scientist refuses to be hindered by stroke |url=http://www.insidebayarea.com/bayarealiving/ci_3771766 |newspaper=InsideBayArea |date=1 May 2006 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20060518185704/http://www.insidebayarea.com/bayarealiving/ci_3771766 |archivedate=18 May 2006 |accessdate=8 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://astro.berkeley.edu/people/marc-davis|access-date=2026-10-18|title=Marc Davis|website=UC Berkeley Astronomy}}</ref>
